result.precedentSearch:
Shift counts: the team has three shapes. (1) Masking: the eight ...ByIntMod32/...ByLongMod64 natives (simpleIntArith.java:337-351, simpleLongArith.java:306-320), Java's << and >>, which rung N's bodies copied and which is why the compiled LSHIFT masked (row 335). (2) Signed counts with an overflow check: intShift, longShift, unsignedIntShift, unsignedLongShift (simpleIntArith.java:365-380, simpleLongArith.java:334-348, simpleUnsignedIntArith.java:203-217, simpleUnsignedLongArith.java:207). These test b < 0 first and saturate a count below -31/-63 before negating. (3) The interpreter's saturation at the width (interpreter/glue/prim/Int.java:173-183, Long.java:183-193). The new natives follow (2) for the negative count, including the far-negative test before -b, and (3) for saturation at the width. They drop (2)'s throw on a lost bit, as decided on 2026-09-22.
Guards: grep -rnE '([a-z]) ?== ?\(?-\1\b' over ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/ finds exactly 16 x==(-x) sites, all in the two edited files: row 333's six and the ten siblings (pre-edit simpleIntArith.java:274,279,284; simpleLongArith.java:71,76,249,253,265,270,275). All 16 are gone. The team's earlier repair of this defect was rung N guarding divisor -1 inside REM (CompilerBuiltin.fss:601, :686), a workaround at the caller. The spelling Integer.MIN_VALUE/Long.MIN_VALUE is already in these files (simpleIntArith.java:258, simpleLongArith.java:229).
Long multiply: four shapes in these files. (a) Guard-and-divide (the two repaired methods). (b) Widen-and-narrow (intOverflowingMul, simpleIntArith.java:74-76). (c) Divide-back with zero on its own line first (unsignedLongOverflowingMul, simpleUnsignedLongArith.java:68-73). (d) longCautiousNonNegativeMul answering factors below 2 first (simpleLongArith.java:96-101). So two of the four already handle zero explicitly. I chose Math.multiplyExact, which the brief offers, over copying (c)/(d) plus a zero line, because shape (a) is also wrong for a product equal to the minimum (measured).
narrow: the wrapping natives jLongWrappingToInt (CompilerBuiltin.fss:51) and jLongWrappingToUnsignedInt (:96; :94 pre-edit) were imported and unused. The interpreter's UnsignedLong$FromLong is (int) x (glue/prim/UnsignedLong.java:230-234), and tests/UnsignedTest.fss:210-211 asserts truncation.
Testing a native no body uses: library_tests/IntegerChoose1.fss:13 imports a simpleIntArith native straight into a test; IntSemanticsRungB does the same for the four unused saturating Div/Abs natives.
Where the fix belongs: the natives plus the prelude bodies (map/spec-to-implementation.md s4.3: the flat ZZ32/ZZ64 traits). INTEGERLITERALFOLDING runs before TYPECHECK (PhaseOrder.java:57,142). Its binary folder (IntegerLiteralFoldingVisitor.java:58-108) does not fold LSHIFT, RSHIFT or narrow, so numeral shifts still reach the prelude. Its unary folder (:150-157) answers -, DOTMINUS and |..| of a numeral exactly, which is why the zero defect only ever showed on variables.

decisions: The shift rule is in four new natives (intBitLeftShift/intBitRightShift, longBitLeftShift/longBitRightShift), not in Fortress bodies over << and >>. The rejected alternative was a four-branch body per operator ('if other >= 32 then 0 elif other >= 0 then self << other elif other <= -32 then self >> 31 else self >> (-other) end'), which needs no Java. Natives were chosen for three reasons: the team's precedent for signed counts is a native (intShift), one native call is the machine shift the decision asks for, and a body adds three compiled comparisons and a negation to every shift.

The natives are named in the Bit family (they sit beside intBitNot/intBitAnd, and the decision calls them 'bit operators'). The rejected alternative was '...ByIntSaturating32' after the neighbouring '...ByIntMod32'. In these files 'Saturating' means clamping to MAX/MIN (intSaturatingAdd), which is a different thing from a shift saturating to 0 or -1.

Math.multiplyExact replaces the guard-and-divide check in longOverflowingMul and longSaturatingMul. The rejected alternative, which the brief also offered, was testing Long.MIN_VALUE plus a zero line. That keeps a second defect: Long.MAX_VALUE/|a| < |b| rejects a product equal to -2^63 (measured: -2^32 * 2^31 threw, probes/IntSemTable-compiled-before.txt:52). multiplyExact is Java 8 and the JVM's own check. The saturating twin catches its ArithmeticException and returns the file's existing sign formula ((a^b) >> 63) ^ Long.MAX_VALUE. The int multiplies widen to long and have no guard, so they were not touched.

The four saturating natives that no prelude body calls (intSaturatingDiv/Abs, longSaturatingDiv/Abs) are asserted by importing them into the test, as library_tests/IntegerChoose1.fss:13 does. The rejected alternative was to fix them with no assertion, since no operator reaches them.

Signed narrow truncates: the rider value set at launch is 'truncates'. So ZZ64.narrow uses jLongWrappingToInt and all five of rung W's assertions are reversed. The tail's sentence 'With signed narrow = unchanged, ...' is the conditional for the other value and was not applied.

Rung W's shouldOverflowZZ32/shouldOverflowNN32 helpers were removed. They are component-private and had no other use (grep over all .fss/.fsi). This follows the brief's 'the shouldOverflow helpers there go if nothing else uses them'.
In the test, 2^31 as a ZZ64 is computed as 2^32 DIV 2 rather than written as the numeral 2147483648, whose bit length is 32. This follows the batch record's warning and the FACTS literal-wrap lines.
